title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: MOE'S COOKIE HOUSE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Moe Brandt, an ironworker from Wilmington, Delaware.
He builds skyscrapers forty stories up.
Then his wife Teresa, an ER nurse, dared his crew to enter the hospital's gingerbread house contest, for the food bank.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SKYSCRAPER
segments.author: Louis Sullivan
lines: Moe drew a gingerbread skyscraper. Forty floors. A working elevator.
Teresa just smiled. Her nurses had won six years in a row.
His old blueprint book had one line circled, from the architect Louis Sullivan:
Form ever follows function.
A gingerbread house is for standing up and making people smile.
So Moe drew a little row house, just like his mom's.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE DOG BOWL
segments.quote: When we build, let us think that we build for ever.
segments.author: John Ruskin
lines: Night one, the crew slapped thin walls together with runny icing.
By morning, the roof was in the dog bowl. The dog was thrilled.
Teresa read them John Ruskin, an English writer on art:
When we build, let us think that we build for ever.
So Moe baked walls as thick as a paperback and mixed icing like mortar.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: BIG HANDS
segments.quote: Architecture starts when you carefully put two bricks together. There it begins.
segments.author: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
lines: Moe's hands are like oven mitts. Every candy cane he touched snapped.
His apprentice Rosie taped up a note from the architect Mies van der Rohe:
Architecture starts when you carefully put two bricks together. There it begins.
So Moe slowed down. Two gumdrops at a time, with tweezers, like steel beams.
Rosie did the fancy icing. Moe did the heavy lifting. Of gumdrops.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE MACHINE
segments.quote: A house is a machine for living in.
segments.author: Le Corbusier
lines: The house looked nice, but it just sat there.
Then quiet Big Hector quoted Le Corbusier, the Swiss-French architect:
A house is a machine for living in.
So they made it live. A door that opens. Tiny lights in the windows. Cotton smoke from the chimney.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE QUIET CREW
segments.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
lines: By week three, they worked in grumpy silence until one in the morning.
Teresa read them a line from Goethe, the German writer:
I call architecture frozen music.
Moe turned on the oldies station. Soon five ironworkers were piping icing to the beat, and Hector was singing. Badly.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE RIBBON
segments.quote: We shape our buildings; thereafter they shape us.
segments.author: Winston Churchill
lines: Contest day. The nurses built a castle with a moat. Moe's crew lost by one point.
Nobody wanted to go home. Rosie quoted Winston Churchill:
We shape our buildings; thereafter they shape us.
That little house had made them a team. Now they eat lunch together, phones down.
And it sold at auction for six hundred dollars, for the food bank.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Build for the job. Build to last. Go slow. Make it live. Add music. Let it shape you.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Build for the job. Build to last. Go slow. Make it live. Add music. Let it shape you.
I built a gingerbread house once. I ate the roof before the icing dried.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
